title: Align a Language Model with DPO
blurb: Train on preference pairs without a reward model: preference probabilities, sequence scores, the DPO loss, training metrics, IPO and per-token drift from the reference.
intro: Direct Preference Optimization turns preference data (this reply is better than that one) into a supervised loss on the policy itself, with the reference model standing in for an explicit KL penalty. The steps build the Bradley-Terry preference model, scoring whole replies with a language model, the DPO loss and its implicit rewards, the reward accuracy and margin used to watch training, the IPO loss that stops the margin running away, and per-token KL to measure how far the policy moved. The capstone takes one DPO gradient step on a tiny language model with a hand-written gradient.
